title: The Opening of Makkah
era: Ten Thousand Fires at Marr az-Zahran
teaser: The city that had driven him out watched ten thousand campfires light the valley above it.

layers.title: The Setting
layers.subtitle: A treaty broken at a well called al-Wateer
layers.content:
Under the terms agreed at al-Hudaybiyah, the Arab tribes could enter alliance with either side, and an act of aggression against an allied tribe gave its protector the right of retaliation. Banu Bakr allied with the Quraysh. Khuza'ah allied with the Prophet ﷺ. For a while they kept the peace.

Old scores from before Islam did the rest. In Sha'ban of the eighth year, Banu Bakr attacked Khuza'ah at a place called al-Wateer, under cover of a dark night, with men and arms supplied by the Quraysh. Pressed hard, the tribesmen of Khuza'ah ran for the Holy Sanctuary, where no blood may be shed. Nawfal, the chief of Banu Bakr, followed them in and killed them there.

The survivors came to Madinah for justice. The Prophet ﷺ put three demands to the Quraysh, any one of which would settle it: pay blood money for the dead of Khuza'ah, or renounce the alliance with Banu Bakr, or accept that the truce was void.

The Quraysh grasped at once what they had done and sent their chief Abu Sufyan to Madinah to renew the treaty. He went first to the house of his daughter Umm Habibah, the Prophet's wife, and moved to sit on the Messenger's bed. She folded it up. When he asked whether the bed was too good for him, she told him it was the bed of Allah's Messenger and he was an unclean polytheist.

He went to the Prophet ﷺ, who gave him no assurance at all. He went to Abu Bakr, who declined. To 'Umar, who refused flatly. To 'Ali, and begged, hinting at mastery over all the Arabs if he would intercede. 'Ali refused too. Abu Sufyan rode home and reported four refusals and one silence. Makkah was disappointed, and still did not expect what was coming.
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The March Nobody Was Told About
layers.subtitle: One intercepted letter and ten thousand men
layers.content:
At-Tabari records that the Prophet ﷺ asked 'Aishah to make the preparations particular to marching out to war three days before any news of the broken covenant reached Madinah. Abu Bakr came in, saw what was being packed, and said it was not the usual time for war. She told him she had no idea.

On the morning of the third day 'Amr bin Salim al-Khuza'i arrived with forty horsemen and laid out what had happened to his people. Budail came after him, then Abu Sufyan, and the report was beyond doubt.

Then came the blackout. In Ramadan an eight-man mission under Abu Qatadah bin Rab'i was sent toward Edam, a short distance from Madinah, purely to pull attention away from the real target. Fear ran everywhere. Hatib, one of the most trusted of the Companions, secretly sent a woman to Makkah with a letter naming the intended attack. Revelation informed the Prophet ﷺ. He sent 'Ali, al-Miqdad, az-Zubair and Abu Marthad after her, and they found the letter after a long search, hidden in the braids of her hair.

Hatib said he had no blood tie with the Quraysh, that his family in Makkah had nobody to protect them, and that he had hoped to earn Makkan gratitude for his children's sake. He swore he had not apostatised. 'Umar wanted to cut his head off as a hypocrite. The Prophet ﷺ accepted the excuse and pardoned him, saying that he was one of those who fought at Badr, and that perhaps Allah had looked at the people of Badr and said: do as you please, for I have forgiven you.

He left on the tenth of Ramadan with ten thousand men, Abu Ruhm al-Ghifari in charge of Madinah behind him.
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Sentence That Decided the Day
layers.subtitle: How a conquest was argued about in advance
layers.content:
Al-'Abbas joined the column at al-Juhfah. At al-Kadeed, a watering place between 'Usfan and Qudaid, the Prophet ﷺ broke his fast and the people broke theirs. They camped for the night in the valley of Fatimah at Marr az-Zahran, and he ordered the men to light their fires. Ten thousand fires came up out of the dark, in full view of the road to Makkah. 'Umar was put in charge of the watch.

Abu Sufyan went out that night with Hakim bin Hizam and Budail bin Warqa' to see what was there. They met al-'Abbas before they reached the camp, and he told Abu Sufyan plainly: accept Islam and persuade your people to surrender, or be killed. The Muslims wanted to kill him where he stood. He was brought before the Prophet ﷺ, who asked him whether it was not time he bore witness to the Oneness of Allah, and Abu Sufyan professed the faith. At al-'Abbas's request he was given a privilege suited to a man who liked to boast: whoever takes refuge in Abu Sufyan's house is safe, whoever stays in his own house is safe, and whoever enters the Sacred Mosque is safe.

Next morning al-'Abbas held him at a place where he could watch the army pass. Tribe after tribe went by with banners raised. Abu Sufyan said no power on earth could withstand these people, that his brother's son's sovereignty had grown too great. It is rather the power of Prophethood, al-'Abbas replied, and Abu Sufyan agreed.

Then Sa'd bin 'Ubadah passed with the banner of the Helpers and called out that today would see the great fight, that there would be no sanctuary at the Ka'bah, that today the Quraysh would be humiliated.
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Revelation
layers.subtitle: Three hundred and sixty idols and four verses
layers.content:
Abu Sufyan reported the threat, and the Prophet ﷺ became angry. Nay, he said, today the Ka'bah will be sanctified and the Quraysh honoured, and he had the banner taken from Sa'd at once and given to his son Qais, or, in another version, to az-Zubair. The Sealed Nectar gives the departure from Marr az-Zahran as the morning of Tuesday the seventeenth of Ramadan, while its own map of the campaign is labelled the twentieth; the day of entry is not agreed.

Four columns went in. Khalid bin al-Walid took the right flank through the lower side of the city, az-Zubair the left flank through the upper side carrying the Messenger's banner, Abu 'Ubaidah the infantry up a side valley. The orders were not to kill except in self-defence. Khalid met the one armed party that had gathered at Khandamah and reached the heart of the town, killing twelve and losing two men. Az-Zubair planted the banner at al-Fath.

The Sacred House held three hundred and sixty idols. He struck them down with his bow, reciting «وَقُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ إِنَّ الْبَاطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقًا» — 'And say: the truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Falsehood is ever bound to vanish.' (17:81) And «قُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَمَا يُبْدِئُ الْبَاطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ» — 'Say: the truth has come, and falsehood can neither create nor restore.' (34:49) He took the key from 'Uthman bin Talhah, went inside, found images of Ibrahim and Isma'il drawing divination arrows, denounced it, and ordered every image erased.
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: What It Left Behind
layers.subtitle: No reproach on you this day, go free
layers.content:
He prayed inside with Usamah and Bilal, then stood in the doorway above the crowd. Every claim of privilege, of blood or property, was under his heel, except the custody of the Ka'bah and the supplying of water to pilgrims. The pride of the pre-Islamic era was abolished: all men descend from Adam, and Adam was made from dust. He recited «إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ» — 'the most honourable of you before Allah is the one most conscious of Him.' (49:13) Then he asked the Quraysh what they expected him to do with them. They said they expected only goodness. He answered with the words of Yusuf to his brothers: «لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ» — 'no reproach on you this day.' (12:92) Go your way, for you are freed. Days earlier, on the road, he had quoted his cousin Abu Sufyan bin al-Harith the same verse.

When the time for prayer came Bilal climbed onto the Ka'bah and called the adhan. 'Attab bin Asid, sitting in the yard, remarked that Allah had honoured his father by sparing him the sound of it. The Prophet ﷺ came over and told him what he had just said. 'Attab and al-Harith bin Hisham professed Islam on the spot.

Nine of the worst criminals were exempted. Ibn Khatal was killed clutching the curtain of the Ka'bah, and Miqyas bin Sababah, who had taken blood money for his brother and then killed the man anyway. Some of the nine were later pardoned. Beyond them the pardons ran wide: Wahshi who killed Hamzah, Hind who chewed his liver, Habbar whose spear killed the Prophet's daughter, Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl who had fought Khalid at the gate that morning, Fudalah bin 'Umair who had planned to kill him mid-circuit.

He stayed nineteen days. Then he went home to Madinah, because the Helpers had begun to fear he would keep the city that expelled him, and he told them he had lived with them and would die with them.

Carry this. He entered with ten thousand and did not settle a single score of his own.
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

quiz.prompt: What act broke the truce of al-Hudaybiyah?

options.text: The Quraysh refused entry to Muslim pilgrims at the appointed time
Banu Bakr, armed and reinforced by the Quraysh, attacked Khuza'ah at al-Wateer and killed them inside the sanctuary
Khuza'ah raided a Qurayshite caravan bound for Syria
Abu Sufyan expelled the Muslim residents remaining in Makkah

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — Banu Bakr attacked Banu Khuza'ah at al-Wateer in Sha'ban 8 AH with men and arms supplied by the Quraysh, and Nawfal pursued them into the sanctified area.
quiz.scholar_reflection: The treaty had made allies into protected parties. Killing Khuza'ah inside the Haram broke two things at once: a signed agreement, and the one rule about that ground that even the pre-Islamic Arabs had kept.

quiz.prompt: What three options were put to the Quraysh after the attack?

options.text: Surrender the killers, pay a fine, or fight
Accept Islam, leave Makkah, or accept siege
Pay blood money for the dead of Khuza'ah, renounce the alliance with Banu Bakr, or accept that the truce was void
Renew the truce on new terms, pay tribute, or hand over Nawfal

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — three demands were made, the acceptance of any one of them being sufficient.
quiz.scholar_reflection: Two of the three cost the Quraysh very little. They took neither, and then sent Abu Sufyan to ask for the treaty back.

quiz.prompt: Hatib sent a letter to Makkah warning of the attack. What happened to him?

options.text: He was executed for treason on 'Umar's advice
He was pardoned, the Prophet ﷺ noting that he was one of those who fought at Badr
He was expelled from Madinah and later readmitted
He fled to Makkah before the letter was recovered

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari, cited in al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — the Prophet ﷺ accepted his explanation and pardoned him, saying perhaps Allah had looked at the people of Badr and said: do as you please, for I have forgiven you.
quiz.scholar_reflection: The letter had already been intercepted, so no harm had landed. What was weighed was the man's whole record, not the worst hour of it.

quiz.prompt: Sa'd bin 'Ubadah announced that the day would bring the humiliation of the Quraysh. What did the Prophet ﷺ do?

options.text: He said nothing, since the banner-bearer spoke only for himself
He confirmed it, but forbade any killing inside the sanctuary
He said the Ka'bah would be sanctified and the Quraysh honoured, and had the banner taken from Sa'd
He replaced Sa'd's whole division with the Emigrants

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — the banner was taken from Sa'd and entrusted to his son Qais, or in another version to az-Zubair.
quiz.scholar_reflection: A slogan shouted on the march can set the tone of an occupation before a single gate is reached. He corrected the sentence and removed the banner in the same breath.

quiz.prompt: How many idols stood in the Sacred House when he entered it?

options.text: Three hundred and sixty
Ninety-nine
Seventy
The sources do not give a number

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — three hundred and sixty idols, knocked down with his bow while he recited 17:81 and 34:49.
quiz.scholar_reflection: He had circled that building as a boy, as a merchant, and as a man being spat at. He cleared it with a bow, reciting a verse about falsehood having no second act.

quiz.prompt: Hatib gave away a military operation to buy safety for his children in Makkah. Where do you land?

options.text: A man's record can outweigh a single act, and his did
Betrayal is betrayal; the pardon was mercy, not justice
The letter failed, so the question is easier than it looks
Anyone with unprotected family is a risk and should never have been told

quiz.slider_label: The record earns pardon — The act demands punishment
quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari, cited in al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — 'Umar wanted him executed as a hypocrite; the Prophet ﷺ pardoned him on the grounds of Badr.
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'Umar's reading was not unreasonable, and he accepted the ruling with the words: Allah and His Messenger know best. Two men can weigh the same act differently and only one of them decides.

quiz.prompt: Preparations for war began three days before any news of the breach reached Madinah. What do you make of that?

options.text: Foresight — the breach was predictable to anyone reading the tribes
Guidance — he was told before he was informed
Routine caution that happened to line up with events
The detail is At-Tabari's, and reports about timing deserve care

quiz.slider_label: Read it as foresight — Read it as guidance
quiz.citation: At-Tabari, cited in al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — 'Aishah was asked to prepare for a march three days before the news of the breach arrived, and Abu Bakr remarked that it was not the usual season for war.
quiz.scholar_reflection: Abu Bakr noticed. That is the most striking part of the account: the man closest to him could not work out what the packing was for.

quiz.prompt: Wahshi killed his uncle. Hind mutilated the body. Habbar's spear killed his daughter. All three were pardoned. Could you have done it?

options.text: Yes — a state cannot be founded on a settling of family scores
No — some acts create a debt no amnesty can cancel
Pardon them publicly, and never trust them again privately
The victims' families should have decided, not the head of state

quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — pardon was extended to Wahshi, to Hind, to Habbar, and to Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl who had attacked Khalid's detachment that morning.
quiz.scholar_reflection: He had ten thousand men in the city and every legal ground he needed. What the day is remembered for is the list of people he let walk.

quiz.prompt: The amnesty was general, and nine men were exempted from it. Is a pardon with exceptions still a pardon?

options.text: Yes — the exceptions are what make the general offer credible
No — once you name exceptions you are holding a trial, not offering mercy
It depends entirely on how the nine were chosen
Some of the nine were pardoned later, so even the list was not final

quiz.slider_label: Exceptions break it — Exceptions define it
quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — the blood of nine of the worst criminals was declared lawful even under the curtains of the Ka'bah, and some of them were later pardoned.
quiz.scholar_reflection: Miqyas bin Sababah had accepted blood money for his brother and then killed the man who owed it. The list was short, and it was about conduct rather than about which side anyone had fought on.

quiz.prompt: The Helpers feared that having taken his birthplace he would stay in it. What is home, in that moment?

options.text: Where you were born — nothing later replaces it
Where you were received when nowhere else would have you
Wherever the work is; attachment to either is sentiment
Both, and the choice between them costs something either way

quiz.slider_label: Where you were born — Where you were received
quiz.citation: al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — he pressed the people of Madinah to explain their fear, then assured them that he had lived with them and would die with them.
quiz.scholar_reflection: He is buried in Madinah. The answer he gave at as-Safa that day was not a diplomatic reassurance; it was a description of what actually happened.
